problem: Offline imitation-learned navigation policies such as NavDP are bounded by their fixed demonstration corpus and suffer covariate shift and compounding errors at rollout. RL avoids this but needs reward engineering and is sample-inefficient.
motivation: Diffusion navigation policies trained on synthetic offline data drift out of distribution near obstacles and produce shaky trajectories. A privileged global planner can label the correct action at every state the policy visits, so DAgger-style online imitation is possible if it can be scaled to high-dimensional visual diffusion policies with massively parallel simulation.
key_idea: Fine-tune a pretrained NavDP diffusion navigation policy in IsaacLab with a DAgger-style rollout-update loop, where a NavMesh global planner labels the policy's own visited states with expert waypoint trajectories and safety scores.
insight: On-policy expert labels give large gains: NavOL scores 69.0 mSR on the new benchmark versus 42.2 for NavDP, and the from-scratch variant already reaches 48.3 with about 1.5% of NavDP's compute. Ablations show that mixing in expert actions during rollout (w/o expert rollout: 43.9 SR vs 69.0) and starting from a pretrained prior (from scratch: 48.3) matter most. Scene diversity also helps (1 scene 57.8, 10 scenes 64.8, 50 scenes 69.0), and the critic adds little (67.1 without it).
method: Model: NavDP-style multimodal diffusion policy with DepthAnythingV2 RGB and depth encoders, 16 fused tokens, and a DiT/DDPM head that outputs 24 relative waypoints (dx, dy, dyaw). A critic sharing the backbone scores trajectory safety, and the top-ranked sample is executed.

Expert planner: NavMesh (Habitat-Sim) shortest path from the current pose to the goal, post-processed by line-search clearance, uniform 0.25 m resampling, cubic spline smoothing and projection back onto the NavMesh. Start-goal pairs are sampled until the raw path has at least 5 keypoints.

Online data aggregation: 128-step rollouts over 256 parallel IsaacLab environments (Dingo robot). The policy action is executed with probability rho=0.8 and the expert trajectory otherwise. Waypoints are tracked by MPC and a low-level controller, and (obs, goal, expert trajectory, safety score) tuples are stored.
Safety target: counts waypoints closer than d_safe=0.5 to an obstacle and adds a clearance-growth term (alpha=0.1), all computed from the NavMesh, to supervise the critic.

Policy optimization: after each rollout, train 10 epochs on only the latest data (batch 2048, lr 1e-5) with the denoising MSE loss plus lambda times the critic MSE. Visual tokens cached during rollout are reused to speed the update.

Scene and domain randomization: 50 re-textured 3D-Front scenes (BlenderProc, rooms stacked into USD assets), randomized camera height (0.25-1.25 m), pitch (-30° to 0°), agent radius and height, and initial orientation. 1,000 iterations on 8 RTX 4090 GPUs take 2 days.
Benchmark: 8 held-out 3D-Front scenes with 100 fixed start-goal pairs each, for zero-shot evaluation.

setting.backbone: NavDP diffusion policy (DepthAnythingV2 ViT encoders + DiT, DDPM) with critic, initialized from NavDP weights and fine-tuned online
setting.training_data: Online rollouts in 50 3D-Front scenes in IsaacLab (about 2,000+ trajectories/hour, ~400 steps each), labelled by a NavMesh planner; initialized from NavDP pretrained weights (large-scale synthetic offline data)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with a point goal
setting.action_space: predicted relative waypoints (24 steps: dx, dy, dyaw), tracked by MPC and a low-level controller
setting.simulator: IsaacLab / Isaac Sim (training and benchmark); NavMesh from Habitat-Sim for the planner
setting.privileged: NavMesh global planner and scene geometry used only during training; none at test time

numbers.extra: trained on 3D-Front scenes in IsaacLab; averaged over Cluttered-Easy, Cluttered-Hard, Intern-Home, Intern-Commercial

numbers_note: Real-world metrics are successes out of 10 trials per scene. Per-scene numbers are omitted from the entries. Benchmarks are custom (NavDP benchmark and the new 3D-Front benchmark), not canonical ones.
results: NavOL reaches 80.4 mSR / 76.3 mSPL on the NavDP benchmark (NavDP 77.8 / 74.8) and 69.0 / 63.7 on the new 3D-Front benchmark (NavDP 42.2 / 37.7). On the real Go2 it succeeds in 25/30 trials versus 8/30 for NavDP.
limitations: Training requires a privileged NavMesh planner, a heavy 3D asset pipeline (BlenderProc and IsaacSim) and 8x RTX 4090 for 2 days.
Real-world failures: the policy exploits gaps at the test-area boundary and misjudges low obstacles (table legs) because of low camera height.
Only point-goal navigation is evaluated, and gains on the NavDP benchmark are small (e.g. Intern-Home is slightly below NavDP).
